summary:
All three rounds pass — no split-brain detected.

**The needle:** `app/cluster/node.go:124` — the quorum check was

```go
if finalVotes >= totalNodes/2 {
```

With 5 nodes, integer division gives `totalNodes/2 = 2`, so a candidate in a 2-node minority partition (its own vote + one peer) satisfied the check and declared itself leader at the same time the 3-node majority elected its own — split-brain. A quorum requires a strict majority, so the fix is:

```go
if finalVotes > totalNodes/2 {
```

Now 3 of 5 votes are required, which only one partition can ever have.

**Verification:** the root-owned `/usr/local/bin/split-brain` binary wasn't writable, so I rebuilt to `~/bin/split-brain` and ran `PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH" /app/test.sh`. Output: minority partition `[0 1]` stalls at 2/5 votes, majority `[2 3 4]` elects node 2 with 3/5, and all rounds report `SAFE` ending in `PASS: No split-brain detected across all rounds`.

One unrelated cosmetic quirk I left alone: the "became LEADER for term 3 with 1 votes" log line has its printf arguments swapped (`finalVotes` and `currentTerm` at `node.go:128`) — it misprints the term/vote numbers but doesn't affect correctness.

The test passes — all three rounds report `SAFE: leader election handles partitions correctly`.

**The needle:** `app/cluster/node.go:124`. The quorum check was

```go
if finalVotes >= totalNodes/2 {
```

With 5 nodes, `totalNodes/2` is 2 (integer division), so `>=` let a candidate win with just 2 votes. When a partition splits the cluster into `[0 1] | [2 3 4]`, node 0 gets 2 votes (self + node 1) and the minority side elects a leader alongside the majority's leader — split-brain. A majority requires strictly more than half, so I changed it to `finalVotes > totalNodes/2` (i.e., 3 of 5). You can see the fix working in the output: node 0 still gets 2/5 votes but no longer becomes leader, while node 2 wins with 3/5 in the majority partition.

**One caveat on verification:** `test.sh` invokes a prebuilt `split-brain` binary at `/usr/local/bin/split-brain`, which is root-owned and I have no sudo, so I couldn't replace it in place. Instead I built the fixed source to `/tmp/bin/split-brain` and ran `PATH=/tmp/bin:$PATH sh /app/test.sh`, which resolves to the fixed binary. If you have root, rebuild it into place with `cd /app/app && go build -o /usr/local/bin/split-brain .`

Unrelated side note I noticed but didn't touch: the "became LEADER" log line at `node.go:128` has its printf arguments swapped (`finalVotes` prints as the term and `currentTerm` as the vote count), which is why the output reads "LEADER for term 3 with 1 votes". Cosmetic only.

Found and fixed the needle — the test now passes all three rounds.

**The bug** was the quorum check in `app/cluster/node.go:124`:

```go
if finalVotes >= totalNodes/2 {   // before
if finalVotes > totalNodes/2 {    // after
```

With 5 nodes, `totalNodes/2` is 2 (integer division), so `>=` let a candidate become leader with just 2 votes. Under a `[0 1] | [2 3 4]` partition, node 0 could win its minority side with 2 votes (itself plus node 1) at the same time node 2 won the majority side with 3 — split brain. A quorum has to be a strict majority, so the comparison must be `>` (i.e., at least 3 of 5).

While verifying, I also fixed a swapped-argument printf on the "became LEADER" line, which was logging the vote count as the term ("became LEADER for term 3 with 1 votes"). That was cosmetic only.

**Verification:** `test.sh` invokes `split-brain` from PATH, but the installed `/usr/local/bin/split-brain` is root-owned and I have no way to overwrite it as the `bench` user. So I rebuilt the binary to `/app/app/split-brain` and ran `PATH=/app/app:$PATH /app/test.sh`, which passed: `PASS: No split-brain detected across all rounds`, with every round electing only the majority-partition leader (node 2 with 3/5 votes) while node 0's 2/5 votes correctly failed. If you rebuild the Docker image, the fixed binary will land in `/usr/local/bin` normally.
